## Abstract  

Major League Baseball's Hall of Fame selection process remains one of the most prestigious yet subjective honors in professional sports.  
In this project, we aim to develop a machine learning model capable of predicting whether a player will be inducted into the Hall of Fame based on career-level statistics and achievements.  
Utilizing the Lahman Baseball Database, which includes detailed player records spanning over a century, we will perform data cleaning, feature engineering, and model training using logistic regression and decision trees.  
Our goal is not only to achieve high prediction accuracy, but also to identify which career metrics most significantly influence Hall of Fame voting outcomes.

## Results

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import joblib
from ipywidgets import Dropdown, Output, VBox

# Load dataset
people = pd.read_csv("data/People.csv")
people['full_name'] = people['nameFirst'].fillna('') + " " + people['nameLast'].fillna('')
player_names = sorted([name.strip() for name in people['full_name'].unique() if name.strip()])

# Load pre-trained model
bat_model = joblib.load("models/batting_model.pkl")
bat_feature_columns = joblib.load("models/batting_model_columns.pkl")

# Load the dataset with all features your model expects
# Replace with the path to the dataset you used for training
stats_df = pd.read_csv("data/batting_hof_elig_transformed.csv")  

# Dropdown and output widgets
dropdown = Dropdown(options=player_names, description="Player:")
out = Output()

def predict_hof(change):
    player_name = change['new']
    with out:
        out.clear_output()
        player_row = people.loc[people['full_name'] == player_name]
        if player_row.empty:
            print(f"{player_name} → Player data not found.")
            return
        player_id = player_row['playerID'].values[0]
        features_row = stats_df.loc[stats_df['playerID'] == player_id]
        if features_row.empty:
            print(f"{player_name} → Stats data not found.")
            return
        
        model_features = features_row[bat_feature_columns]
        pred = bat_model.predict(model_features)[0]
        result = "Predicted: Inducted" if pred == 1 else "Predicted: Not Inducted"
        print(f"{player_name} → {result}")

# Observe dropdown changes
dropdown.observe(predict_hof, names='value')

# Display dropdown and output
ui = VBox([dropdown, out])
ui
```
